facts.statement: Pulchrapollia lived during the Early Eocene in the United Kingdom and the United States.
facts.quote: Pulchrapollia is an extinct genus of halcyornithid bird from the Early Eocene London Clay of Walton-on-the-Naze, United Kingdom and the Nanjemoy Formation of Virginia, United States.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Pulchrapollia was discovered in 1978 near Walton-on-the-Naze in the London Clay.
facts.quote: The holotype of Pulchrapollia was originally found in 1978 by a collector near Walton-on-the-Naze in Bed A, a Ypresian sediment of the London Clay, a fossil-rich formation.

facts.statement: Dyke and Cooper described the type species Pulchrapollia gracilis in 2000.
facts.quote: In 2000, BMNH A 6207 was described as the type species Pulchrapollia gracilis and assigned to the Psittaciformes by Dyke and Cooper.

facts.statement: Mayr and Kitchener described the species Pulchrapollia tenuipes in 2023.
facts.quote: In 2023, Mayr and Kitchener described Pulchrapollia tenuipes based on NMS.Z.2021.40.65.

facts.statement: Pulchrapollia was a small bird roughly the size of a red-fronted parakeet.
facts.quote: Pulchrapollia was a small bird, about the size of the red-fronted parakeet.

facts.statement: Pulchrapollia possessed zygodactyl feet with two toes pointing forward and two pointing backward.
facts.quote: Like other halcyornithids, Pulchrapollia had zygodactyl feet, with two toes facing forward and two facing back on each foot.

facts.statement: Halcyornithids, the family to which Pulchrapollia belongs, are considered basal relatives of both parrots and songbirds.
facts.quote: Halcyornithids are regarded as basal relatives of both parrots and songbirds.

facts.statement: Pulchrapollia was initially classified as a stem-parrot distinct from the Halcyornithidae family.
facts.quote: Pulchrapollia was initially described as a psittaciform stem-parrot, and indeed was regarded as distinct from the Halcyornithidae.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the smaller braincase of Pulchrapollia compared to other halcyornithids might represent an increase in encephalization over time.
facts.quote: It is possible that this difference represents an increase in encephalisation among halcyornithids over time.

rejected.statement: The holotype of Pulchrapollia eximia includes a neurocranium that is significantly smaller than those of other halcyornithids.
rejected.quote: The holotype of Pulchrapollia eximia preserves a neurocranium, which is much smaller than that in other halcyornithids.
